subject.title: docs(durable): rebuild beta3 durable core RFC and proof plan

question: Should OpenClaw publicly adopt this narrowed cross-owner durable-core RFC as the intended beta3 architecture?
rationale: The contributor has resolved the mechanical documentation problems, but deciding whether the remaining cross-owner contract belongs in core determines the direction of several dependent persistence and runtime changes.

options.title: Sponsor the narrowed RFC
options.body: Approve the residual cross-owner contract and use this stable RFC as the boundary for reviewing dependent implementation work.

options.title: Keep owner-specific durability
options.body: Decline a shared core layer and continue extending the existing task, subagent, delivery, audit, lease, and flow owners independently.

options.title: Pause the durable stack
options.body: Leave the architecture unpublished until a smaller demonstrated runtime gap establishes the need for a shared contract.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the narrowed RFC
recommendation.body: Approve the residual cross-owner contract and use this stable RFC as the boundary for reviewing dependent implementation work.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history spans subagent persistence, restart-sensitive session state, and cross-cutting repository product direction.
